repairs.description: Crossan treats the feeding story as a parable of divine justice: whether historical or symbolic, it charges church leaders to ensure that everyone has food.
repairs.rationale: This complete sentence preserves both the story's parabolic interpretation and the practical obligation that Crossan draws from either reading.

repairs.description: Crossan reads Emmaus as a parable in which Jesus becomes recognizable through scripture and hospitality toward a stranger, rather than through a literally shape-changing resurrection body.
repairs.rationale: This complete sentence captures Crossan's preferred narrative meaning while retaining his contrast with a literal account of bodily transformation.
